items.title: Upcoming badge
items.summary: Upcoming Badge is a widget for Mac OS X Dashboard. Use it to view your Upcoming.org events watch list using Dashboard. Simply enter your username on the flip side of the widget. Links www.gingerbeardman.com/upcoming/

items.title: Katamari Damacy iPod Color
items.summary: I hacked my last iPod Color using AlterPod so that I get the Prince of All Cosmos instead of the standard no entry sign. The iPod was later stolen, returning the little Prince to live amongst the stars!

items.title: Ceefax Viewer
items.summary: Ceefax Viewer is a widget for Mac OS X Dashboard. Ceefax (phonetic for “See Facts”) is the BBC’s teletext information service. Teletext is an information retrieval service provided by television broadcast companies. Teletext pages can be viewed on television sets with suitable decoders. They offer a range of text-based information, usually including nationa…

items.title: Wire Hang Redux
items.summary: I made a new game! It’s a from-scratch remake of an original Java game, Wire Hang, by Masaki Kobayashi (D2AC) who went on to become part of the Gran Turismo team. I had a pretty underpowered laptop at the time, and writing my own version of the game was the only way I was able to play it comfortably. My version of the game, Wire Hang Redux—made with Kobaysh…

items.title: JUS4QIX: the story of a classic arcade video game
items.summary: I’m a big fan of the 1981 arcade game QIX . Back in 2003 tracked down the author of the game, Randy Pfeiffer, who had moved on from the video game industry to run his own business creating CAD software for model railway enthusiasts. I asked him some questions about the game and he was gracious enough to answer, albeit a little puzzled why anybody would want…

items.title: Early morning disco
items.summary: Spring morning sun coming through my blinds, across my sofa, onto my disco ball. Taken with a FujiFilm FinePix 1400 Zoom , which at 1.3 megapixels saved photos at 1280×960 pixels!

items.title: Circuit Heat
items.summary: I made a prototype of a game called Circuit Heat. It is a version of the classic network completion puzzle (aka Pipes, FreeNet, Net, NetWalk, etc). The graphics remind me a little of the Atari Lynx classic puzzler Chip’s Challenge. Notes: At this time, long before iPhone, I was playing Java games on a (Sagem?) cell phone so many of my concepts around this t…

items.title: Terra Firma
items.summary: This is my entry into the BlitzCoder Stupidest Game Competition, 2002. You need to guide a sky diver—whose parachute has failed—past obstacles and attempt to land on a cow. Fun! It was written using BlitzBasic and later recompiled in BlitzPlus. This is the game that made me realise I could make games. Archived web page: gingerbeardman.com/archive/terrafirma…

items.title: Sensible Soccer T-shirt
items.summary: I won a competition in a magazine that resulted in my design for a Sensible Soccer T-shirt being put into production by a company called Joystick Junkies. By early 2004 they were available to buy at online from the BSI Merch website and Amazon UK, as well as on the UK high street at all River Island stores, and to buy wholesale from Big Ben Interactive. T-s…

items.title: Yaking
items.summary: A small prototype for a kayak/canoe “simulator” game, featuring water currents, a gate to paddle through, and somewhat unique paddling controls (press left/right alternately). Made using BlitzBasic and targetting Game Boy Advance resolution of 240×160. Archived web page: gingerbeardman.com/archive/yaking/ Download: gingerbeardman.itch.io/yaking

items.title: Web Design Index 2
items.summary: A couple of websites I’ve built: one for photographer Rankin and the other for my former employer Form, made during my time working for them in 1998/9, are featured in the book Web Design Index 2 and on the accompanying CD. Compiled by Günter Beer, and published by The Pepin Press/Agile Rabbit Editions. Links www.webdesignindex.org www.amazon.co.uk/Web-Desi…

items.title: Bendertron
items.summary: This is my Futurama-themed fan-game inspired a little by the Williams arcade classic Robotron and a lot by Jeff Minter’s Llamatron. Written in BlitzBasic for Windows 9x. Created in Feb/Mar 2001 during the dot-com boom and released in Jan 2002 after the bubble burst! Explosion animation by the wonderful Alex Amelines Sounds and graphics ripped from the TV sh…

items.title: Simple Soccer
items.summary: Simple Soccer is my take on the classic Sensible Soccer. It was written in BlitzBasic and ran at 800×600 under Windows 9x. I built multiple parts—player control, dribbling, cpu and formation, goalkeeper behaviour—but never managed to combine it all in a finished game. Still, I count it as my first real game. Archived web page: gingerbeardman.com/archive/soc…

items.title: My old Atari ST software
items.summary: I dug out some old 3.5” double density floppy disks from my Atari ST days and have made some old apps of mine available as downloads. These were made between 1992 and 1994. Chaos Calc 2 (fractal viewer) REview (text document viewer) Paint (chunky pixel art app) Also included are some ST icons and Fuji Bar! , a companion app for the PaCifiST emulator on Wind…

items.title: Quick Paths
items.summary: Whenever you want a file, you first have to find the folder it is in, which is a faff if that folder is nested several levels deep. Quick Paths lives in the system tray and jumps you to a favourite folder with one click: into the topmost file selector, into Explorer, or into ZipMagic’s Archive Manager. If none of those are open, it launches a new Explorer w…

items.title: My old Windows software
items.summary: After moving to Windows PC from Atari ST I discovered Visual Basic and my mind was blown by the possibilities of laying out a graphical user interface using the mouse and adding code to make it do stuff. I jumped in and made a whole bunch of Windows software, including some world-first features like hot-corners to invoke the screen saver and being able to q…

items.title: Fuji Bar!
items.summary: Fuji Bar! is a system-tray shell for the PaCifiST Atari ST emulator under Windows 95. Serious use of PaCifiST means editing .ini files a lot; this lets you change the usual settings through a GUI and launch the emulator in one click. About 76k of RAM. Version 1.34. New: Laptop, Parallel and STe directives, plus the Image directive’s drive qualifier. Works w…

items.title: SaveAble!
items.summary: SaveAble! adds hot corners to Windows. Shove the mouse into a corner to kick the screen saver on immediately (leaving your desk, sensitive stuff on screen), or to stop it coming on at all (a long compile, a download, anything the saver would only hinder). Plus version includes a system tray icon. This is the first hot-corners implementation I know of on Win…

items.title: Wobble!
items.summary: Wobble! shakes the screen until it looks like jelly. Severity from a slight judder to near-earthquake, optional colour invert / screen flip, slow motion, desktop preview, password, and context-sensitive help. Version 1.40. New: wobble a custom picture, severe slow-motion option, multi-tasking-friendlier, settings dialog tweak. Recompiled with Visual Basic 5…

items.title: WINotes
items.summary: WINotes is a Post-it-style sticky notepad for the Windows desktop. Multiple notes at once, each with its own size, colour and typeface; sticky or not; load and save (optionally as plain text); file association; spawn another note; load back from the previous session; optional on-screen hotkeys; choice of alarm sound. Version 1.73. 16-bit and 32-bit. Recompi…

items.title: Stars!
items.summary: Stars! turns your monitor into a portal to another galaxy. Eight directions of travel, configurable star count and parallax levels, three star shapes, desktop preview, context-sensitive help, and Windows screen saver password support. Version 1.14. Visual Basic, Windows 95/NT. Uses about 60k. Pairs nicely with SaveAble! if you want hot corners. 1.14: passwo…

items.title: ST Icons
items.summary: An icon library for Atari ST emulation under Windows 95. 32×32 and 16×16, 16-colour icons for use with PaCifiST (and later bundled with Fuji Bar!). A .reg file assigns the right icons to TOS programs and .st / .msa disk images if you copy the library into C:\Windows\ . Archived page: gingerbeardman.com/archive/tektonix/icons.htm

items.title: Cease & Desist: The Designers Republic
items.summary: A letter I received from The Designers Republic after creating a font inspired by their work. They chose to order a cease and desist, rather than fostering creativity. Matt Sephton created an original font called Block Out–a techno font that can still be found here. He had used Fontographer. It was, as he put it, influenced by the tDR font in the Wipeout se…

items.title: Day
items.summary: Day is a day-by-day alarm and reminder. It sits on the taskbar (or hide it with Ghost) and pops up when you asked it to. Alarms can repeat once, daily, weekdays, weekly, monthly or yearly, with an optional five-minute early warning. Version 1.33. New: Dawn, a tiny starter you put in Startup instead of Day itself, so you get a yes/no prompt at boot. Written…

items.summary: I wrote a video game FAQ and uploaded it to GameFAQs: gamefaqs.com/console/psx/file/wipeout_xl.txt

items.title: Ghost
items.summary: Ghost hides and shows any running Windows application. Pick a task from the list and click Hide or Show. Hiding Program Manager clears every desktop icon in one go, which is a quick way to tidy a messy desktop. Version 1.10 for Windows 3.1x. You can also launch it with a command-line prefix to pre-select a task, e.g. GHOST.EXE Ti . Archived page: gingerbear…

items.title: Messages
items.summary: Messages is a small utility for leaving notes for other people who use the same PC. Handy if you are sharing a machine with Windows 95’s multi-user password facility. It manages multiple message files and uses Notepad to edit them. Version 1.11, 16-bit and 32-bit builds. Visual Basic. Windows 3.1x and 95/NT. Archived page: gingerbeardman.com/archive/tektoni…

items.title: MsgBoxer
items.summary: MsgBoxer generates Visual Basic MsgBox code to your exact specification. Pick the icon, buttons, default button and modality in a dialog, hit Test, then paste the snippet into your app from the clipboard. Now with context-sensitive help. Version 1.11b, 16-bit and 32-bit. Windows 3.1x and 95/NT. This is a tool I wrote because I was tired of looking up the Ms…

items.title: Light!
items.summary: Light! is a screen saver that passes a trailing beam across the desktop, illuminating whatever is behind it. You can change the size and speed of the light, and whether it inverts the screen colours. Version 1.30 is a rewrite: faster, smaller, and with a password. Written in Visual Basic for Windows 3.1x. Featured on the TECH Win (ASCII, Japan) cover CD, No…

items.title: Tektonix Menu 2
items.summary: Tektonix Menu 2 is a tiny, fully customisable menu system for MS-DOS. It uses less than 8k of memory when fully utilised, which makes it ideal for launching games and other memory-hungry DOS programs. Works in a Windows 95 DOS box too. Version 2.01. Also in the zip: a mouse prompt helper, a PCX viewer, a reboot utility, and a small DOS paint tool. Archived…

items.title: Paint
items.summary: A simple paint program for children, for the Atari ST. One colour for each mouse button. Sixteen-colour ST-low, a two-row palette, fill, shift, line, box, circle, spray, a couple of picture buffers, and load/save of .MAT files. Shareware, developed 1992–94. This is version 1.02 from the nostalgia pack I later put up for PaCifiST. The pack includes a sample…

items.title: REview
items.summary: REview is a small ASCII file viewer for the Atari ST, written in GFA BASIC 3.5. It exists because the desktop’s built-in Show is not enough once you have a stack of coverdisk docs and want to search, bookmark, or print a paragraph. Find and repeat-find, ten bookmarks, goto line, block start/end, print block or whole document, toggle scan rate, and a 24-line…

items.title: Chaos Calc 2
items.summary: Chaos Calc 2 is my GEM-based Mandelbrot explorer for the Atari ST, written in GFA BASIC 3.5 and compiled. Zoom (almost) into infinity, cycle colours, swap palettes, and save plots as compact Chaos Definition Files or uncompressed Degas pictures. Shareware. Registration is £5, which unlocks Julia sets, extra CDF saves, colour-cycle direction, and desktop acc…
